descriptionChirho: A heap or mound, typically of water (as in the parting of the Red Sea or the Jordan) or of ruins. Both clusters describe the same concrete noun with S116340 simply adding the comparative preposition ke- ('as a heap'). Multilingual evidence is uniform: eng 'heap/as-a-heap', spa 'montón/como-montón', hin 'ढेर/जैसे-ढेर', arb 'رُكاماً/كَالنَّدِّ', kor '더미/무더기-같이', swa 'lundo/kama-chungu'. All point to the same sense of a piled-up mass.
